commit message:
Add a tutorial notebook for data consumers

This is the hands-on material for the fairgraph part of the "EBRAINS Knowledge Graph for data consumers" tutorial. It covers reading metadata only: connecting, finding research products by id, name, DOI and property filters, following forward and reverse links, looking up controlled terms, and downloading files. Creating and saving metadata is left to the companion tutorial for data providers.

Sections 7 to 10 are marked optional and cover local JSON-LD snapshots with Collection, custom queries, release status and spaces, and error handling.

The notebook targets the production Knowledge Graph, and runs end to end on fairgraph 0.13.3, which the EBRAINS-experimental kernel in the EBRAINS Software Distribution currently has, as well as on 0.15.0 and on the development version. The handful of cells needing something newer than 0.13.3 - Regex filters, the case_sensitive option of by_name(), Equals, sort_property, and reloading a Collection from a file - check for it first and print a message rather than failing.

author: Andrew Davison
commit message:
Add a tutorial notebook for data providers

This is the hands-on material for the fairgraph part of the "EBRAINS Knowledge Graph for data providers" tutorial, covering the writing side: building nodes, validating them locally, saving them, and understanding how fairgraph decides between creating a node and updating an existing one. It ends with a complete dataset, the curation workflow, bulk upload with Collection, and a cleanup section. The companion notebook for data consumers covers reading.

Files are not registered one by one: the notebook describes a FileRepository pointing at a Collaboratory bucket and notes that the Knowledge Graph ingests the files it finds there. Creating File nodes by hand is kept as an optional section, for repositories the service does not cover, together with the reason it is slow.

Everything writes to the pre-production Knowledge Graph, in the user's private "myspace", so that nothing participants create reaches production. The example dataset is deliberately fictional.

Verified by running every cell against fairgraph 0.13.3 with openMINDS 0.5.1, against 0.15.0, and against the development version. The stored outputs come from 0.15.0, since the existence-matching behaviour demonstrated in section 4 differs between released versions and the unreleased exact-matching work.

author: Andrew Davison
commit message:
Match existence queries exactly by default, and add an existence_match option

The existence query used by exists() and save() filtered string properties with the KG's CONTAINS operator, so a new Dataset called FOO was identified with an existing one called FOO-BAR and silently overwrote it (#149). Existence queries now use EQUALS, which the KG applies case-insensitively but not whitespace-insensitively, so a stored name with a trailing space is no longer found by a local name without one.

exists() and save() take a new existence_match argument, either "equals" (the default, matching name_matching.MATCH_TYPES) or "contains" to restore the old behaviour; save() passes it on to child objects. The save cache holds a match found with "contains" under a separate key, so that it is not later returned for an "equals" lookup. Collection.upload() does not expose the option and always matches exactly.

The exact match is implemented by a new Equals filter value, the counterpart of Regex, which selects the EQUALS operator in place of CONTAINS. It is exported from fairgraph and documented in the API reference and the queries guide. A list of Equals values is not supported and falls back to CONTAINS, as for Regex (#150).

MockKGClient in test/utils.py gained matching case-insensitive EQUALS handling.

commit message:
Add --norm-multiallelic to vcfputtogetheragain; docs and separate test

--norm-multiallelic mirrors `bcftools norm -m-`: instead of the zig
semantics (drop the ALT alleles of multi-allelic input records from
the merged record while keeping their renumbered genotypes - the
source of the invalid MULTI=ALTPROBLEM records), all ALT alleles are
spliced into the merged record and genotype renumbering uses the
cumulative allele offset of the preceding records. Merged records
then always satisfy the VCF spec; MULTI=ALTPROBLEM remains and now
exclusively marks true genotype conflicts (a sample called for two
different alleles across overlapping records).

Measured on samples/scaffold612.phased.vcf: the 256 previously
invalid ALTPROBLEM records now validate cleanly (vcfvalidate reports
0 errors).

Docs: --norm-multiallelic documented in vcfputtogetheragain.md, the
vcfcreatemulti.md ALTPROBLEM caveat now points at the alternative,
and the tool docs are copied into doc/ by the build (added
vcfputtogetheragain.md and the new test doc to the copy list).

Tests: separate doctest file test/pytest/vcfputtogetheragain-norm.md
(runs the tool with --norm-multiallelic on the scaffold612
mini/region extracts and test-dup, with regression baselines)
asserting that all generated outputs validate cleanly - including
the records that fail validation in default mode. Default (zig
parity) behaviour is unchanged. All 14 CTest tests pass.

* Fix crashes with vectorized bicop parameters

`dbicop(u, "clayton", parameters = <n x 1 matrix>)` errored with
"parameters exceed lower bound ... actual: 4.77025e-310", a subnormal double
(a read of uninitialized memory). bicop_wrap() reduced vectorized parameters
with `par = par.topRows(1)`, an Eigen self-aliasing assignment: the resize
frees par's buffer before the copy, so the Bicop was constructed with garbage
and check_parameters threw at construction. Only one-parameter families with a
positive lower bound (clayton/gumbel/joe) surfaced it; gaussian/frank swallowed
the garbage. Fixed with `.eval()`.

Also update the vendored vinecopulib sources (companion upstream PR
vinecopulib/vinecopulib#700):
- abstract.ipp: the discrete per-row evaluation leaves indexed the parameter
  matrix out of bounds for parameterless (independence) and nonparametric (tll)
  copulas; broadcast unless there is one parameter set per row and guard the
  empty-parameter case.
- parametric.ipp: check_parameters_size() validates rows and cols
  unconditionally, so a transposed same-size shape can no longer reach the
  coefficient-wise bound checks (an out-of-bounds read under NDEBUG).

Add a regression test over all one-parameter families (vectorized vs
row-by-row) plus the reported clayton case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Take the upstream fix for Joe's tau at its removable singularity

tau(theta) = 1 + 2 [psi(2) - psi(2/theta + 1)] / (2 - theta) is 0/0 at
theta = 2: the bracket and the denominator vanish together. The quotient was
evaluated directly, so par_to_ktau(bicop_dist("joe", 0, 2)) returned NaN and
the surrounding neighbourhood lost most of its significant digits to
cancellation. theta = 2 is an ordinary interior point that a user can specify
directly or reach from a fit.

Fixed upstream in vinecopulib/vinecopulib#758, which is merged; this vendors
that change verbatim so the header tree stays a faithful mirror. The limit is
1 - psi'(2) = 2 - pi^2/6, covered near the singularity by a series expansion
that agrees with the closed form to about 1e-10.

The R-level test pins the limit and compares the expansion against the closed
form at 1e-8, a threshold that sits between the correct expansion and a sign
error in the psi''(2) term.

Note that editing a vendored header does not trigger recompilation: src/*.o
must be removed by hand.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add vcov() and confint() for copula parameters

Assembles a covariance matrix from the observation-wise scores and the
derivatives of the estimating equations, with methods for bicop_dist,
vinecop_dist and vine_dist, and derives Wald intervals from it. Rows and
columns are named by tree, conditioned pair and conditioning set, so a
coefficient can be located in the model without counting.

The orientation of the bread matters and is easy to get wrong. hessian()
returns d sbar / d theta. Under step_wise = TRUE -- the default -- that is the
Jacobian of the step-wise estimating equations, not a Hessian: it is exactly
block upper-triangular, because the pseudo-observations entering each pair
copula depend on the parameters of earlier trees. So the M-estimation bread is
A = -t(H), the sandwich is A^-1 B A^-T / n, and the matrix must not be
symmetrized first -- doing so discards the cross-tree propagation terms.

Monte Carlo against the true sampling distribution (1200 replications,
four-dimensional Gaussian D-vine, n = 400) puts the standard errors within
2.4% throughout, and coverage of nominal 95% intervals at 0.941-0.955.
Symmetrizing the bread instead inflates the tree-one standard errors by up to
7% and pushes their coverage to 0.964.

type = "model" returns A^-1/n, which relies on the information equality and so
holds only for a maximum-likelihood estimator; it is refused for
step_wise = TRUE. Nonparametric pair copulas are refused outright, since no
derivatives are implemented for them. Discrete variables are allowed: the
backend falls back to central finite differences, which agree with a numerical
gradient of the vine log-likelihood to a relative 4e-5.

Neither variant accounts for estimation of the margins, which makes the
intervals somewhat too short; this is documented.

Documented as `parameter_uncertainty` alongside the other grouped topics, with
the method aliases, and added to the pkgdown reference index next to mBICV.

* Drop type = "model" and the vine_dist methods

Two simplifications from review.

The model-based form A^-1/n needs the information equality A = B, which holds
only at a maximum-likelihood estimator -- so not for the default step-wise
objective, where A is a Jacobian rather than a Hessian. The sandwich is correct
either way, so offering only the sandwich removes an argument, a branch and an
error path without losing anything valid. R/vcov.R loses about half its body.

The methods for vine distributions are removed. They treated the copula data as
observed, which quantifies uncertainty in the pair-copula parameters *given* the
margins; a vine() fit estimates its margins too, and the second stage inherits
the first stage's variability. The experiment reported in the manuscript puts
the cost at about three percentage points of coverage. Correcting for it needs
the influence function of the marginal estimator, and fit_margin() is a
user-supplied black box, so there is nothing to differentiate. Better to provide
no method than a silently anticonservative one; the documentation gives the
bootstrap recipe instead.

commit message:
Accept shared immutable payloads in async HTTP requests

Change `TRequestData`'s `Content` field from `TString` to `TBlob`. This is done to avoid dependency on `TString`'s atomic counter in the face of the future `std::string` migration.

`Content` is chosen to be migrated to `TBlob` since this one is usually the largest string in the request. In the case of multiple requests with the same body (e.g. sharding) the cost of copying is quite noticeable.

Also move out the TStringStream object which stores the entire http request.

Verification: 61 NNeh/async tests passed in each string mode. Shared/legacy, binary/empty POST, snapshot replacement, cancellation/error and caller-owner release are covered. Scatter async suite passed; affected Scatter/YT/YaIO consumers compiled.

YT Scatter suite has 12 existing failures. With the changes stashed, the Host failure and HandleError/SendingTimeout/ReplyHeaders failure classes reproduce on baseline.

NO_COW measurement: 64 copies of a 1 MiB request body allocate zero additional payload buffers instead of 64. Including final HTTP framing: 65 -\> 1 large allocations (68,158,104 -\> 1,048,728 bytes). One final contiguous wire buffer remains.

author: shanalyb
commit message:
Don't abort when socket() fails in NAsio::TTcpAcceptor::Bind

Refs #1765.

If `socket()` fails in `TTcpAcceptor::TImpl::Bind`, the error is stored in `ec` but the function keeps going with fd -1. `CheckedSetSockOpt` then throws inside a `noexcept` method and the process aborts with `setsockopt() failed for reuse addr`. This happens on kernels booted with `ipv6.disable=1` and when the process runs out of file descriptors. The fix adds the missing `return`.

This doesn't fully fix the issue: the tcp2 server still tries to bind both `0.0.0.0` and `::`, so on nodes without IPv6 the worker still fails to start, just with a regular `TSystemError` instead of an abort.

Tested on a machine with `ipv6.disable=1`: without the fix `THttpListen::TEchoTest` aborts with the error from the issue, with the fix it fails with a regular exception. The other neh tests that don't need IPv6 pass.
